set.body:
Defect: D5/D6 at the cell level. Revision 1's UndeclaredEncoding fired only when two encodings fit, which leaves a single-fit column silently guessed -- and an Excel serial 1.000983796296296 parses perfectly well as a decimal, so the defect survived the fix.

Do: Cell.integer/decimal/text/stamp, each REQUIRING a declared encoding from the profile. No declaration -> unconditional refusal NoDeclaredEncoding(at, column). Genuine ambiguity is a profile-validation error, not a cell error. MinuteDotSecond and ExcelSerialDays are cell encodings, not clock units -- there is no ClockUnit enum.

Tests: Table-driven over the measured hazards: '1' vs 1.0 (Friends WhichStoryline has every code as both); 6.1000000000000005 as MinuteDotSecond (FilmFest); 1.000983796296296 as ExcelSerialDays (Friends); '2'..'17' in a column declared binary (Friends False memory?); a column with no declaration.

Mutants (SD1 — each must die, recorded by name): let Cell.integer fall back to toDoubleOption.map(_.toInt) -> the '1'/1.0 test must fail. Make an undeclared column guess -> the no-declaration test must fail.

Exit: No reader path can guess an encoding.

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-17-annotation-intake-contract.md S2 'Cells'
set.title: intake P1: typed cells -- an undeclared encoding is a refusal, not a guess
